summary: This is the traditional first program in any language: it displays the text "Hello, World!" on the screen. In Python it takes exactly one line, with no setup or boilerplate around it.

lines.text: A complete Python program can be a single line. There is no class to declare and no main function to define 	op from top to bottom, which is a large part of why Python is a good first language.
print is a built-in function, so it is always available without importing anything. The parentheses after the name are how you call it, and whatever you put inside them is what gets displayed.
Text in Python must be wrapped in quotation marks, which makes it a string. Without the quotes Python would read Hello as the name of something you had defined earlier and report an error.
